subject: business-studies
topicDisplay: Operations Finance And Influences On Business
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Reducing a business's environmental impact might involve:
options: Recycling, cutting waste and using renewable energy
questions.explain: Businesses reduce environmental impact through recycling, cutting waste and using cleaner energy.

options: Hiring as many workers as possible
Producing output using the fewest resources and least waste
Always producing the cheapest possible product
questions.explain: Efficiency means getting the most output from the available inputs while minimising waste.

questions.q: What is a drawback of holding too much stock (overstocking)?
options: Money tied up in stock and higher storage and waste costs
questions.explain: Holding excess stock ties up cash and increases storage, insurance and potential wastage costs.

options: The total amount of stock held
Output produced per unit of input (e.g. per worker) in a given time
questions.explain: Productivity measures output per input, such as the number of units produced per worker per hour.

questions.q: Globalisation has made it easier for businesses to:
options: Trade and operate across international borders
questions.explain: Globalisation has increased trade and the ability of firms to operate across countries.

questions.q: Why can a profitable business still run out of cash?
options: Customers may pay later while the business must pay its own bills now
Profit is always paid in cash immediately
Profit and cash are the same thing
questions.explain: Profit and cash differ in timing; a firm can be profitable yet short of cash if money comes in slowly.

questions.q: How can new technology act as an external influence on a business?
options: It removes the need for any staff
It always lowers all costs immediately
It never changes how businesses operate
It can create new products and ways of selling but requires investment
questions.explain: Technology creates new products and selling methods but often needs investment and training to adopt.

questions.q: What does Just In Time (JIT) stock management aim to do?
options: Keep stock levels to a minimum, with materials arriving as needed
Hold very large stocks at all times
questions.explain: JIT keeps stock to a minimum, with supplies arriving just as they are needed, reducing storage costs.

questions.q: What does TQM (Total Quality Management) involve?
options: Every employee taking responsibility for quality
Only the quality team checking products
Checking quality only at the end of production
questions.explain: TQM is an approach where everyone in the business is responsible for maintaining quality.

options: A rise in average cost per unit as output increases
A fall in average cost per unit as output increases
questions.explain: Economies of scale mean the average cost per unit falls as a business produces on a larger scale.

questions.q: Flow production is most suitable for:
options: Mass-producing large quantities of identical, standardised products
questions.explain: Flow (mass) production continuously makes large quantities of identical products, e.g. cars or canned drinks.
